name: serpentine-four-sections
prompt: fixture_serpentine_four_sections.py has four differential pairs across the board on L1, each held to 300 ps pad to pad with 1 ps of skew, longer than the straight run. Route each pair on L1 and let the router add the length in a section between x = -12 and x = 12 that may meander up to 2 mm beyond the pair's own copper. Give each section its own meander setting: the pair at y = 15 keeps its meander at least 3.0 mm pitch; the pair at y = 5 uses 0.4 mm deskew bumps, the pair at y = -5 0.6 mm bumps, and the pair at y = -15 keeps its bumps 2.0 mm apart. Do not draw any of the meanders or bumps yourself.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components e6bf1cb (the installed package in the eval venv, 2.0.1.dev74+ge6bf1cbc2) and import no jitxexamples.patterns module; the fictional parts in cl_parts.py need no parts database. The fixture module is fixture_serpentine_four_sections.py, Design SerpentineFourSectionsDesign. Each pair carries ConstrainDiffPair(...).timing(300 +/- 2 ps).timing_difference(1 ps).structure(DIFF_100); the straight 40 mm path is 250 ps at DIFF_100's 160 mm/ns. Rows 5, -5 and -15 start at StaggeredPairChip, 2.0 mm out of skew, so their sections carry deskew bumps on one trace. The working chain is the one in jitxexamples' serpentine_sections example (wave lane R): PairInsertion(invert=True) to PairPoint(invert=True), the section between two PairPoints with Route.Config(envelope_overhead=2.0), then PairPoint to PairInsertion, every control point PortAttached to its pair; each section carries its own tag and a design rule on the tag (serpentine_params(min_pitch=3.0), coupled_pair_params(deskew_bump_radius=0.4 or 0.6), coupled_pair_params(min_bump_spacing=2.0)). The check scores min_pitch as a lower bound, and deskew_bump_radius and min_bump_spacing to the prompt's values; spike C3 found min_radius and max_bump_length not held on jitx 4.6.0, so they are not asked for. Provenance for the radii: on this fixture, deskew_bump_radius 0.2 realized 0.275, the same radius the bumps take on a row with no radius rule, while 0.4 and 0.6 realized exactly; what sets that floor is not established, so the prompt asks only for 0.4 and 0.6. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Write the layout in the fixture module, fixture_serpentine_four_sections.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name, SerpentineFourSectionsDesign. Do not move or remove the fixture's chips, pairs or constraints, and do not change the substrate or its structures. Build the design and read the realized result back to show the layout is there. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each piece of layout you wrote with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: Per pair, a chain of code routes through two PairInsertions and two PairPoints at x = -12 and 12, the section between the pair points configured with Route.Config(envelope_overhead=2.0) and tagged, one design rule per tag; a build with every delay and skew met; COMPLETION.md with each section's measured pitch, bump radius or bump spacing.

assertions.text: each row has one configured coupled section within 2 mm beyond the pair's copper; row 15's meander pitch is at least 3.0, rows 5 and -5 have bumps of 0.4 and 0.6 radius to three decimals, row -15's bumps sit 2.0 apart along the pair; delay and skew raise no issue, and no copper is drawn in code
each setting is a design rule on a tag carried by that pair's section only, not a board-wide rule that would also change the other pairs
COMPLETION.md reports each section's realized pitch, bump radius or bump spacing read back from the captured arcs, not only that the rules were written
if COMPLETION.md mentions min_radius or max_bump_length, it does not claim either holds without a measurement showing it
COMPLETION.md gives, for each piece of layout the prompt asked for, the electrical or fabrication need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
